page: OVHcloud c3-64-flex is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by KVM virtualization. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor family operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. Configured without simultaneous multithreading at one thread per core, the hardware eliminates resource contention between virtual execution threads. It is provisioned with 64 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core, along with a bundled 50 GB local NVMe solid-state drive and 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results confirm strong multi-core processing capabilities across varied computational tasks. The c3-64-flex achieved top-quartile performance in multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Clang software compilation tests. Memory subsystems demonstrated top-tier tier results in the PassMark memory evaluation alongside strong small-block cached read throughput, though uncached memory read bandwidth registered in the mid-tier. Parallel execution tasks such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, ray tracing, and Redis operations all scored within the top 25% of measured systems, whereas single-threaded throughput and larger-model language generation demonstrated mid-tier performance.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation provides consistent compute power per resource unit without the jitter typical of shared or hyperthreaded environments. The primary architecture tradeoff is the relatively modest 50 GB local NVMe disk and 64 GB total memory footprint, which bounds the instance to workloads that do not demand extensive in-memory footprints or large local storage arrays. OVHcloud c3-64-flex is engineered for parallel compute tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch data processing, distributed microservices, and medium-scale caching databases.
description: OVHcloud c3-64-flex is a compute-optimized cloud server driven by a 32-core AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring a non-multithreaded setup with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, it pairs 64 GB of system RAM with a 50 GB local NVMe SSD and a 4 Gbps baseline network link. Across empirical benchmarks, the instance demonstrates upper-quartile parallel throughput, excelling in multi-core compilation, ray tracing, PassMark CPU evaluations, and multi-threaded decompression tests. The 1:2 RAM-to-CPU ratio and modest boot-tier local storage prioritize raw computational efficiency over massive memory capacity or high-volume on-disk storage. As a result, the c3-64-flex is well suited for CPU-heavy tasks such as continuous integration build runners, batch transformation jobs, mathematical modeling, and distributed microservice infrastructure.
